chapter: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
title: Jabbo Smith quitting and fear of false teeth
summary: Dickenson doubts Jabbo stopped because of dental work, and says many players perform as well with false teeth if they keep trying.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Jabbo stopped playing not too long after the Hopkins band broke up, I guess.

I don't know why Jabbo stopped playing. Really, I don't. I think it was a matter... I think he had some work done on his teeth. That kind of frightens the guys, you know... But it needn't to be threatening, because they can fix your teeth so that you can play. I know several great musicians that are playing just as great with their teeth...with their false teeth -- playing just as great. And looking just as great with their false hair on their heads! [LAUGHS] You know what I mean?
Right. Well, I guess they're afraid that it will change their embrochure and...

Well, what difference... If they're not using the embrochure, why not try it? That's all I can say. If you're not using it nohow, your band's(?) not going to use it anyway. Why not try it? Just keep trying it. When a guy first starts out, he ain't got no chops. You know?
He's got to work up and make chops for himself. Put the horn where it's comfortable on your mouth, and play it.
